Middle East.headline: Gaza — UNRWA staff member killed in Israeli strike
Middle East.body: An Israeli strike in Jabalia, Gaza, killed one staff member of the UN agency for Palestinian refugees (UNRWA) and injured three others. The interim UNRWA Commissioner-General stated that the personnel were conducting regular duties at a water well to deliver critical services to the community when the attack occurred.

Middle East.headline: Yemen — More than 360,000 displaced amid rising civilian casualties
Middle East.body: Over 360,000 people have been displaced in Yemen since August, according to the International Organization for Migration. Taiz governorate has absorbed the highest number, hosting approximately 145,000 displaced individuals. The UN Human Rights Office has verified 323 civilian casualties since August. Additionally, military sources reported that recent Houthi attacks killed two civilians and injured eight others in Taiz.

Middle East.headline: Middle East — Maritime shipping disruptions threaten food supplies in Yemen and Sudan
Middle East.body: The World Food Programme warned the UN Security Council that attacks on grain ships and maritime disruptions in critical choke points, including the Strait of Hormuz and Bab Al-Mandeb, are worsening hunger in Yemen and Sudan. The agency noted that up to 10 million tonnes of wheat may fail to reach global markets this year due to transit blockages, calling for a humanitarian mechanism to restore food transport routes.
verified_figures: 10 million tonnes of wheat potentially blocked from world markets

Middle East.headline: Bahrain — Two injured in Iranian strikes amid regional escalation
Middle East.body: Bahraini authorities confirmed that two individuals sustained injuries following Iranian strikes targeting the island nation. The incident occurred amid heightened security alerts across the Persian Gulf, marking an escalation in regional hostilities as neighboring states face the spillover of broader geopolitical confrontations involving Iran and various regional and international actors.

Americas.headline: Haiti: UN chief condemns Haiti attack that killed 47
Americas.body: At least 47 people, including at least five children, were killed and more than 50 others kidnapped by armed men in Haiti on Sunday, the United Nations confirmed on Tuesday. The incident, which took place in Kenscoff on the outskirts of the capital, Port-au-Prince, is believed to be one of the largest mass kidnappings in the troubled Caribbean country in recent years. In a video posted on social media, a gang leader threatened to murder hostages if Haiti's National Police kill any of his men in an attempt to rescue people. "If any of our soldiers are hurt, I will kill all of them," he said.

Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: Why the Ebola Outbreak Keeps Growing, According to Virus Expert Pardis Sabeti
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: The ongoing Ebola outbreak centered in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is now the second largest on record. The virus has infected more than 11,000 people in five countries and has killed more than 5,700 people as of Nov. 20. Pardis Sabeti, a leader at the Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard who specializes in computational genetics and evolutionary biology, has tracked Ebola outbreaks for years. In the largest Ebola outbreak on record, in West Africa from 2014 to 2016, she sequenced many of the viral samples from patients, which helped scientists understand how the virus was spreading. Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: The current Ebola outbreak is growing faster than any outbreak of the disease ever. How...
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: For Marie-Roseline Bélizaire, a typical day starts around 6 A.M. at a health center in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, where she pores over freshly confirmed Ebola cases that have come in overnight. From then on, the work is nonstop: she calls dozens of provinces, visits health centers, supervises contact tracing, trains emergency workers and woos donors—as well as any number of other urgent tasks—before she falls asleep and does it all again the next day. Bélizaire, emergency director for the World Health Organization’s Regional Office for Africa, does not expect this work to let up anytime soon. Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: Ebola Outbreak With 50% Death Rate Is Getting Worse: Three Key Reasons Why
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: Ongoing wars, distrust in authorities and difficult terrain is majorly disrupting efforts to defeat the Ebola outbreak which has a death rate of almost 50 percent. Some 5,678 (48 percent) of the 11,613 confirmed Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) resulted in death as of November 17, the most recent date for which the World Health Organization (WHO) has recorded data. The outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo virus, was declared in May and is now described by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) as the second-largest on record.
